chapter: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
title: Brother Bud in a nursing home and Joe's stroke
summary: Crawford wants to interview Bud, who has a good memory; his wife explains Joe's stroke two years earlier damaged his memory.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, well you can see him. He's in the home on uh, Jackson and uh, Brainhardt.
Well I'll stop by there and find out if it'd be alright for us to bring the tape recorder.
Yeah, he's up on the second floor. He'd be glad to see you.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: Boy, he can give you some dates and time.
Yeah, because he's got a good memory. My memory's very bad.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: See, he had, since he had the stroke in the head. He had a stroke of the head two years ago. And he's, uh, mind don't uh, you know, just keep it going all the time. You just gotta stop to think of what it is and what it ain't. He gets tired. Yeah, yeah. The doctor said the brain had been injured and he didn't know to what extent. That's why sometimes he can remember and sometimes he doesn't.
